newsitem.title: USA: USW Coast crudes ease, trade thinned by scheduling.
newsitem.headline: USW Coast crudes ease, trade thinned by scheduling.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes eased early Wednesday, tracking a downward drift in marker West Texas Intermediate (WTI) while activity turned light as traders prepared October pipeline nominations.
"Pipeline scheduling is probably the biggest thing right now," said a refinery trader.
With October flows starting on the first, traders need to make sure supply was in balance, traders said. Potential existed for last-minute deals to meet shipping obligations.
Meanwhile, cash November WTI fell as much as 25 cents from yesterday to $23.90/23.95 early.
With differentials unchanged from the last October deal and a 30-cent roll against November, buyers claimed the market was indicated at minus $2.60.
Line 63 remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for October delivery.
California heavy crude Kern River was unchanged despite prospects for last minute deals ahead of pipeline scheduling. Levels held at $16.15/16.35 a barrel.
And prices for lightly traded Wilmington crude oil held at $17.60/17.70.
